description: A product multiplies the sides of a box into its volume
code:
sides = [2, 3, 4]
volume = sides.product()
assert(volume, 24)
sides.push(0.5)
volume

description: An empty list multiplies to one, the empty product
code:
factors = []
scale = factors.product()
assert(scale, 1)
factors.push(3, 4)
scale

description: A selector compounds growth rates over periods
code:
rates = [0.5, 0.25]
growth = rates.product(rate -> 1 + rate)
assert(growth, 1.875)
rates.push(-0.5)
growth

description: A population product gives the chance that every independent part works
code:
class Part(name, works):
    this.name = name
    this.works = works
Part("pump", 0.5)
valve = Part("valve", 0.75)
chance = Part.product(part -> part.works)
assert(chance, 0.375)
valve.works = 1
Part("seal", 0.5)
chance

description: A class-level rule multiplies each instance's own list of factors
code:
class Box(name, sides):
    this.name = name
    this.sides = sides
$Box.volume = $Box.sides.product()
crate = Box("crate", [2, 3, 4])
cube = Box("cube", [3, 3, 3])
crate.sides.pop()
[crate.volume, cube.volume]

description: A filtered population product in a class-level rule follows new instances
code:
class Trip(name):
    this.name = name
class Leg(trip, onTime):
    this.trip = trip
    this.onTime = onTime
$Trip.chance = Leg.filter(leg -> leg.trip == $Trip).product(leg -> leg.onTime)
home = Trip("home")
Leg(home, 0.5)
Leg(home, 0.5)
assert(home.chance, 0.25)
away = Trip("away")
assert(away.chance, 1)
Leg(away, 0.75)
[home.chance, away.chance]

description: A product converts its values to numbers as multiplication does
A selector that is not a function raises a TypeError while a product without one multiplies the items
code:
xs = [2, 3]
message = ""
try:
    xs.product(5)
catch error:
    message = error
[xs.product(), message]

description: An undefined factor keeps a standing product unknown until it is defined
code:
items = [{q: 2}, {}]
total = items.product(item -> item.q)
assert(total, null)
items[1].q = 5
total

description: A failed update through a product rolls back
code:
def checked(chance):
    if chance > 1:
        throw "NOT_A_CHANCE"
    return chance
odds = [0.5, 0.5]
both = odds.product(checked)
try:
    odds.push(3)
catch error:
    pass
[odds.length, both]

description: A class name runs the population product beside an instance method named product
code:
class Lens(power):
    this.power = power
    def product(other) => this.power * other
wide = Lens(2)
Lens(3)
zoom = Lens.product(lens -> lens.power)
[zoom, wide.product(5)]

description: A product counts the combinations of independent choices
code:
courses = [3, 4, 2]
meals = courses.product()
assert(meals, 24)
courses.push(5)
meals
